title: arXiv physics daily — Fri, 13 Nov 2026
global_caveat: arXiv provides no official trending chart. This inferred ordering is a shortlist of notable recent papers, not a popularity measure; the batch is fresh and citation evidence is limited.

sections.title: Observation of Genuine Multi-Time Quantum Memory
sections.abstract: The authors derive a three-time witness for quantum memory that pairwise tests miss, and demonstrate the hierarchy in a time-continuous superconducting-qubit experiment.
sections.claimed_result: The authors show a minimal qubit example whose every pair of times has a classical-memory explanation, while a joint three-time test certifies quantum memory.
sections.evidence_type: experimental; time-continuous superconducting-qubit realization with time-independent couplings, supported by an analytical witness and channel tomography
sections.unique_caveat: The authors leave open how much additional memory information can be extracted from the full continuous dynamics; this is a proof-of-principle platform demonstration, not a general scaling result.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: An analytical witness is tested experimentally on a superconducting-qubit platform, directly connecting quantum-information criteria to open-system dynamics.

sections.title: JWST Rocky Worlds DDT Observations of LTT 1445 A b and c in Secondary Eclipse Using MIRI/F1500W
sections.abstract: Three JWST/MIRI eclipse visits, combined with prior spectra and radial velocities, indicate that nearby rocky planet LTT 1445 A b has no substantial atmosphere, while the sibling planet c remains weakly constrained.
sections.claimed_result: The authors infer a CO2 partial pressure below 0.6 mbar and surface pressure below about 0.1 bar for planet b; the eclipse of c is too uncertain to establish its atmosphere.
sections.evidence_type: observational; JWST MIRI/F1500W secondary eclipses, prior JWST spectra, and a joint fit including 220 radial velocities
sections.unique_caveat: Planet c’s potentially grazing eclipse and overlapping events leave its eclipse depth poorly determined; planet b’s atmospheric limits depend on retrieval and forward-model assumptions.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Three independent reductions and a joint analysis strengthen the eclipse constraint; independent specialist discussion and science-media coverage appeared shortly after posting.

sections.title: Observation of the Λ(1520) suppression in Pb-Pb collisions at √sNN = 5.02 TeV
sections.abstract: ALICE reports a central-to-peripheral suppression of the Λ(1520)/Λ yield ratio in Pb-Pb collisions and compares the trend with statistical-hadronization and hydrodynamic-plus-transport models.
sections.claimed_result: The measured suppression fraction is 0.589 ± 0.015 stat ± 0.086 syst; the authors find MUSIC coupled to the SMASH hadronic afterburner reproduces the trend within uncertainties.
sections.evidence_type: experimental; ALICE Pb-Pb collision data at √sNN=5.02 TeV, measured across six centrality classes and compared with models
sections.unique_caveat: The role of late-stage rescattering is inferred through model comparison rather than isolated experimentally; the suppression measurement carries an 8.6% systematic uncertainty.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The authors report a 6.8σ result, call it the first observation of resonance suppression within one collision system, and note submission to PRL.

sections.title: The full Gaia colour-magnitude diagram with white dwarfs reveals a declining Milky Way star formation history
sections.abstract: A self-consistent population-synthesis fit to Gaia DR3 main-sequence and white-dwarf stars favors an early-peaking, subsequently declining local Milky Way star-formation history with two recent bursts.
sections.claimed_result: The authors’ 18-parameter CALOMERA fit reproduces counts within 3% in each colour-magnitude region and recovers a declining star-formation history with bursts near 2.4 and 0.5 Gyr ago.
sections.evidence_type: observational; Gaia DR3 photometry and astrometry, interpreted with a semi-analytic chemo-dynamical population model and three white-dwarf cooling libraries
sections.unique_caveat: The inferred early history is conditional on stellar-evolution and cooling prescriptions; the paper reports faint-end discrepancies and does not include binary evolution.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Joint fit to 7.98 million Gaia DR3 stars, including 110,000 white dwarfs; cross-listed across Galactic and stellar astrophysics and discussed by specialist outlets.

sections.title: Euclid data release 1 (DR1) - SIR spectroscopic calibration
sections.abstract: The Euclid SIR paper describes the calibration pipelines used for Data Release 1’s slitless spectra and reports that the validated products meet current wavelength- and flux-calibration requirements.
sections.claimed_result: The authors say the DR1 calibration products and resulting spectra meet mission requirements, while identifying areas for further optimization.
sections.evidence_type: observational; Euclid/NISP slitless spectroscopy and SIR calibration products for DR1
sections.unique_caveat: This is a calibration and data-readiness paper, not a new dark-energy constraint; downstream scientific accuracy remains dependent on calibration performance.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: A major survey collaboration reports calibration infrastructure underpinning more than 170 million validated spectra; cross-listed in instrumentation and cosmology, submitted to A&A.

sections.title: The Gator low-background spectrometer: readout upgrade and photomultiplier tube radioassay for XLZD
sections.abstract: An upgraded Gator high-purity germanium spectrometer adds waveform-level noise rejection and reports radioassay results for photomultiplier tubes intended as XLZD candidates.
sections.claimed_result: The authors report 2.14 ± 0.22 keV FWHM at 2614.5 keV and a 238U/232Th activity reduction by a factor of three in the tested improved-stem tubes.
sections.evidence_type: experimental; low-background high-purity germanium measurements at Gran Sasso, including radioassay of 16 Hamamatsu R17317 photomultiplier tubes
sections.unique_caveat: The stated sensitivity is for a specified sample geometry, and the tubes are candidate photosensors; the paper does not establish background performance for a complete XLZD detector.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Reports measured energy resolution and background figures and assays 16 tubes; cross-listed in nuclear experiment and instrumentation.

sections.title: Performance of the ATLAS tau trigger in Run 3 and future prospects
sections.abstract: ATLAS describes its hadronic-tau trigger algorithms and reports Run 3 efficiencies and simulation correction factors, alongside prospective improvements tested in selected 2026 chains.
sections.claimed_result: The authors report plateau efficiencies of 90–98% and Monte Carlo correction factors of 0.95–1.05 with 2–3% uncertainties over a wide tau transverse-momentum range.
sections.evidence_type: experimental; ATLAS proton-proton collision data from Run 3 at √s=13.6 TeV, with correction studies using 2022–2023 data and selected 2026 test chains
sections.unique_caveat: The efficiency range applies to the plateau region and the reported 2026 improvements were evaluated in selected test chains, not presented as a full future-trigger deployment.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Reports measured Run 3 performance at 13.6 TeV and quantifies efficiency corrections with uncertainties; paper is submitted to JINST.
